SECANT PILING

Working Beside Existing Buildings: Questions for a Secant Piling Brief

Make neighbouring structures a visible part of the scope from the first enquiry.

In this insight

Treat the neighbour as a project interfaceEstablish what is knownDefine communication and evidenceCarry the interface into procurementFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Treat the neighbour as a project interface

An existing building beside a proposed excavation introduces information and coordination needs that extend beyond the retaining wall itself. The project team may need to understand foundations, sensitive uses, access rights and existing condition. A buyer should not assume that a wall method alone resolves those questions. Bring the relevant survey, structural and geotechnical disciplines into the brief at the appropriate stage.

Establish what is known

Create a schedule of available drawings, inspections, condition surveys and ownership boundaries. Distinguish verified information from assumptions about adjoining foundations. Where access is needed to obtain information, identify who will arrange it and how it affects the programme. An unanswered request for neighbour access can become a critical dependency, even when the contractor is otherwise ready to mobilise.

Define communication and evidence

Agree how observations, complaints or changes will be recorded and escalated. The monitoring approach and response criteria belong with the responsible engineers; the client’s role is to ensure that responsibilities and communication routes are explicit. Keep baseline information available to the team that will review later observations. Photographs should have dates and locations so they provide context rather than a disconnected image archive.

Carry the interface into procurement

Tender documents should make neighbouring-asset constraints visible to all bidders. Ask each bidder to explain the consequences for access, sequence, equipment and working hours. Resolve responsibility for surveys and monitoring instead of leaving it under a broad phrase such as protection of adjacent property. A clear allocation supports a fair price comparison and gives the delivery team a practical starting point for coordination.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Separate verified neighbour information from assumptions.
  • Assign access and survey responsibilities.
  • Include communication routes in the delivery plan.
